name: Kitten TTS 2 (mini / nano / pico)
purpose: Tiny CPU text-to-speech: Mini has 82M parameters, 16 languages and 118 voices at 24 kHz and runs from ONNX with int8 (82.7 MB) or int4 (47.5 MB) weights without PyTorch (card). The card states no further motivation.

license.name: Apache-2.0
license.notes: Card says Apache-2.0 for models, voice packs and bundled code (sentence read in the card's License section; no LICENSE file found at the expected path).

architecture.kind: small neural TTS exported to ONNX (82M parameters in the mini)

variants.format: ONNX int8 (82.7 MB), int4 (47.5 MB) and float32 safetensors 0.33 GB
variants.notes: repo total; nano repo 0.78 GB and pico repo 0.35 GB per HF API, contents not inspected

strengths: German has four dedicated voices (Lena, Greta, Jonas, Felix); English voices can also speak German by passing language=de
weaknesses: No quality benchmark (WER, MOS) on the card
Tiny models usually trade naturalness for size; not measured here
best_for: lightweight CPU speech output for assistant replies

tona_fit.reason: Cheapest German-capable TTS in the sweep (Apache-2.0, under 100 MB, CPU), useful as a fallback voice; naturalness unknown, no numbers. Compare against kokoro-82m (record exists) by listening test.

open_questions: Sizes and quality of nano and pico
